tool_input.description: Probe actual createNumber behavior for ambiguous decimal strings
Write probe Java source to scratch temp directory

result:
Created `src/test/java/org/apache/commons/lang3/math/NumberUtilsAgentTest.java` with 56 self-contained JUnit 5 test methods covering `NumberUtils`'s constants, comparisons, `create*`/`toScaledBigDecimal`/`to<Type>` conversions, `isCreatable`/`isDigits`/`isNumber`/`isParsable`, and all `min`/`max` array and 3-arg overloads — including null, empty-array, NaN, and malformed-input edge cases. All 56 tests pass via `./_tools/test.sh`, with no other files modified.

Note: one assumption I had to verify empirically — `NumberUtils.createNumber` returns a `Float` (not `BigDecimal`/`Double`) for plain decimals like `"1.5"` and `"1.23"` when the float/double string forms agree, and `isParsable("1.5F")` is `true` since `Double.parseDouble` accepts the trailing `F`/`D` suffix. I probed actual behavior (via temporary `System.out.println` debug statements inside the test file, removed afterward) rather than guessing, since no other files could be created in the sandboxed `--restricted` environment.
